4. Deepen your SEO Knowledge Building an SEO Team

Ready to scale your SEO efforts by building a high-performing team? Whether you’re hiring your first SEO specialist or expanding an enterprise function, knowing how to structure and grow an SEO team is critical for long-term success.

Building an SEO team goes beyond filling roles—it involves defining responsibilities, aligning with business goals, and creating processes that support collaboration and adaptability. From hiring technical SEOs and content leads to integrating analytics and outreach functions, each decision influences your team’s effectiveness and scalability.

Explore the following resources in this lesson to learn how to build, structure, and manage an SEO team that drives measurable results and adapts to the evolving search landscape.

Frequently Asked Questions on Building an SEO Team

Core SEO team roles typically include an SEO Manager/Lead, Technical SEO Specialist, Content Strategist, and Link Building Specialist. Depending on company size and needs, you may also need SEO Analysts, Local SEO Specialists, or International SEO Experts. Start with versatile team members who can wear multiple hats, then specialize as you scale.

Scale your SEO team by first documenting processes and workflows, then identifying bottlenecks in current operations. Hire based on skill gaps rather than just headcount, prioritize candidates with complementary skills, and establish clear growth paths. Consider starting with contractors or agencies for specialized needs before committing to full-time hires.

Beyond technical SEO knowledge, look for analytical thinking, communication skills, adaptability, and curiosity. Strong candidates demonstrate proficiency with SEO tools, data analysis capabilities, basic HTML/CSS understanding, and the ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders. Cultural fit and collaborative mindset are equally important.

SEO teams can be structured as centralized (one team serving all departments), decentralized (SEO specialists embedded in different teams), or hybrid models. Consider your company’s size, goals, and existing structure. Most successful teams maintain dotted-line relationships with content, development, and product teams while reporting to marketing or growth leadership.
